openFem3d.title: 3D frame
openFem3d.axisHelp: Left: select · box → window, ← crossing · drag wheel: pan · right: rotate (around the selection) · wheel: zoom at cursor
openFem3d.nodeHelp: Node: click in the canvas; existing nodes and grid lines snap into place, otherwise the node lands on the work plane.
openFem3d.beamHelp: Beam: click the start and end points; existing nodes and grid lines snap into place, otherwise the point lands on the work plane.
openFem3d.plateHelp: Plate: click line points, choose Arc edge for a curve; close at the first node.
openFem3d.plateArcHelp: Arc edge: click a control point and an end point; choose Plate to draw the closing edge.
openFem3d.openingHelp: Opening: click line points, choose Arc edge for a curve; close at the first node.
openFem3d.openingArcHelp: Opening arc: click a control point and an end point; choose Opening to close it.
openFem3d.supportPlacementHelp: Support: click a 3D node (or right next to it), a beam (it is split there), a plate (new node in the mid-plane) or empty canvas (new node on the work plane); also a node in the Explorer. Esc or Select to stop.
openFem3d.springPlacementHelp: Spring: click a 3D node (or right next to it), a beam (it is split there), a plate (new node in the mid-plane) or empty canvas (new node on the work plane); the spring gets the last used stiffness, adjust it in the properties panel. Esc or Select to stop.
openFem3d.beamEndHingeHint: Member-end hinge: click a member near the end that should connect with a hinge; My and Mz are released there, a second click fixes them again. Torsion stays as it is.
openFem3d.beamEndHingeHelp: Member-end hinge: click a member close to the end that should connect with a hinge; My and Mz are released there (a small white ball in front of the node), a second click fixes them again. Esc or Select to stop.
openFem3d.pinBeamsToColumnsHint: Pin beams to columns: every end of a beam (including a sloping rafter) on the top of a column gets My and Mz released; the columns stay continuous, and so does a beam carrying a column or a foundation grid under a column base. A cantilever or canopy that hangs only from the column stays fixed. For the selected members, or for all members when no member is selected.
openFem3d.pinBeamsToColumnsNone: No member end changed: no beam connects to a column, or those ends were already pinned.
openFem3d.pinBeamsToColumnsScopeAll: In the whole model (no member selected).
openFem3d.pinBeamsToColumnsSkipped_one: {{count}} beam end stayed fixed: the part behind it would otherwise only be held by hinges and start to rotate (for example a cantilever or canopy).
openFem3d.pinBeamsToColumnsSkipped_other: {{count}} beam ends stayed fixed: the part behind them would otherwise only be held by hinges and start to rotate (for example a cantilever or canopy).
openFem3d.connectNodesHint: Connect nodes to members: every member with a node lying on it (within the connection tolerance of its axis, not right next to a member end) is split at that node; loads, hinges, section, elastic foundation and group carry over. A node just off the axis is not moved: the parts run to the node. For the selected nodes and members, or for the whole model when no node or member is selected; a selected member counts with its start and end node (a column thus connects with its base to the beam below). One undo step.
openFem3d.connectNodesDone_one: {{count}} member split at the nodes lying on it
openFem3d.connectNodesDone_other: {{count}} members split at the nodes lying on them
openFem3d.connectNodesNone: No node lies within {{mm}} mm on a member without being connected to it.
openFem3d.connectNodesScopeSelection_one: Within the selection ({{count}} node or member).
openFem3d.connectNodesScopeSelection_other: Within the selection ({{count}} nodes and members).
openFem3d.connectNodesScopeAuto: Automatically after the change; Undo reverts both. To turn it off: Display tab, Merge and connect nodes automatically.
openFem3d.connectNodesScopeImport: After the import; Undo restores the model as it came in.
openFem3d.mergeNodesHint: Merge nodes: nodes within the connection tolerance of each other (default 5 mm, Display tab) become one node; the node with the lowest number keeps its position. Members, plates, supports, loads, diaphragms and load panels follow; a member of length 0 disappears and a duplicate member remains once, with the loads of both. Whatever cannot be resolved unambiguously (different levels, profiles or springs, a plate that would no longer be flat) is refused per group, with the reason. For the selected nodes (with the end nodes of selected members and the corners of selected plates), or for the whole model without a selection. One undo step.
openFem3d.mergeNodesNone: No nodes lie within the tolerance of each other.
openFem3d.mergeNodesBeamRemoved_zero: Member {{beam}} got length 0 and was removed.
openFem3d.mergeNodesBeamRemoved_one: Member {{beam}} got length 0 and was removed, with {{count}} load.

openFem3d.mergeNodesFailed_other: {{count}} groups of nodes could not be merged

mergeNodesRefusal.diaphragmHeight: Nodes {{nodes}}: diaphragm {{diaphragm}} would no longer lie at one height (more than 1 mm difference).
mergeNodesRefusal.springs: Nodes {{nodes}}: both have a spring in {{dof}}; choose yourself which spring remains.
mergeNodesRefusal.beamProperties: Nodes {{nodes}}: member {{other}} would coincide with member {{beam}}, but they differ in {{properties}}.
mergeNodesRefusal.beamExcluded: Nodes {{nodes}}: member {{other}} would coincide with member {{beam}}, but load panel {{panel}} excludes only one of them.
mergeNodesRefusal.plateCorners: Nodes {{nodes}}: plate {{plate}} would keep fewer than three corners.
mergeNodesRefusal.plateLoop: Nodes {{nodes}}: the edge of plate {{plate}} would touch itself.
mergeNodesRefusal.plateArc: Nodes {{nodes}}: an arc in the edge of plate {{plate}} would no longer be an arc.
mergeNodesRefusal.plateNotPlanar: Nodes {{nodes}}: plate {{plate}} would no longer be flat.
mergeNodesRefusal.openingCorners: Nodes {{nodes}}: opening {{opening}} of plate {{plate}} would keep fewer than three corners.
mergeNodesRefusal.openingLoop: Nodes {{nodes}}: the edge of opening {{opening}} of plate {{plate}} would touch itself.

report.title: 3D calculation report
report.heading: 3D frame calculation
report.pendingHint: The model input below can be printed. Second-order, buckling and member results are not yet available.
report.platesResultsNote: Nodal values per plate in plate axes (z = plate normal); moments positive for tension at the bottom face. MITC4 quadrilaterals of the external 3D engine; first order.
report.edgeSupportsNote: An edge support restrains the listed global degrees of freedom at every analysis node on that edge of the plate mesh.
report.surfaceNote: Intensities in kN/m² and global axes X/Y/Z.
report.nodalNote: Forces in kN; moments in kNm. Global axes X/Y/Z.
report.memberLoadNote: Intensities in kN/m. Local: member axes y/z. Global: axes X/Y/Z, per metre of member length or per projection (per metre of projection perpendicular to the load direction).
report.pointLoadNote: Forces in kN and local member axes y/z.
report.thermalNote: Temperature differences in K; gradients follow the local cross-section axes.
report.checksRunning: The code check is in progress…
report.noSteel: No checkable steel catalogue profile present.
report.governingSubchecks: Governing partial checks per concrete member
report.noConcrete: No concrete member with a valid cross-section and reinforcement cage present.
report.reactionsNote: Forces in kN; moments in kNm. Local member forces follow the local member axes.
report.loadPanelDerived: Derived loads from the load panels
report.windPressureDerivationMissing: The pressure derivation is missing for {{n}} older wind load panels; regenerate the wind loads.
report.internalPressureDerivationMissing: The c_pi derivation is missing for {{n}} older wind load panels; regenerate the wind loads.
report.loadPanelNote: A load panel has no stiffness. Before the analysis its load is converted into the member and nodal loads above, with the factor of the displayed state; p acts in the load direction of the panel.
report.nearlyVertical: Member {{id}} is nearly but not exactly vertical (|cos| = {{cos}} to Z): its local y/z axes are close to where the reference direction switches. Make the member exactly vertical or give it a roll angle.
report.envelopeNote: Minima and maxima across the combinations actually calculated, separately for ULS and SLS. Member forces include stations between the ends; x is measured from the member start. A missing combination result is not treated as zero.
report.continuousNote: Elements with the same non-empty name are combined only when they form one straight, connected chain with the same local axis direction. x is measured from the start of the whole chain; bends and branches remain separate.
report.horizontalNote: Per SLS combination the node with the largest ratio u_hor / (h/300); h is the height of that node above the lowest support. u_hor = √(u_x² + u_y²). Only nodes on a storey level or in a diaphragm count; an intermediate node of a column or facade post does not.
report.ucGroupsTitle: Unity checks per group and profile
report.alphaCrNote: αcr is the first buckling factor of the calculation. According to EN 1993-1-1, 5.2.1(3), an elastic first-order analysis is sufficient when αcr ≥ 10; below that, second order (P-Δ) is required. A red αcr for a first-order analysis falls below that limit.
report.tensionOnlyNote: Tension-only members only take part in a load case or combination while they are in tension; the solver solves each combination separately, with its own set of active members.
report.tensionOnlyFitNote: Tension-only members are fitted after the permanent load: their stress-free length follows the deformation under the permanent load cases (factor 1.0, including self-weight and load panels). The fitting elongation Δ0 per member and the number of fitting calculations are listed with the messages.
report.crossRuleNote: Cross rule: of two tension-only members that cross each other, the one with the largest axial force always stays active, even with a small compressive force. The number of crosses that needed the rule and the largest compressive force are listed with the messages.
report.beddingNote: Winkler foundation: the soil supports the member with springs k·b along its whole length; the solver subdivides the member itself. w is the settlement (positive downwards), p the line load of the soil on the member and p/b the ground pressure under the contact width b. With compression only, "without contact" is the part of the length where the springs dropped out.
report.plateBeddingNote: Winkler foundation: the soil supports the plate with springs k·A on the nodes of the mesh, perpendicular to the plate; A is the tributary area of the node. s is the settlement (positive into the soil), p the ground pressure k·s. With compression only, "without contact" is the part of the plate area where the springs dropped out.

trekSchijf.tensionOnlyHint: Only acts while the member is in tension, like a round-bar wind brace. If a load case or combination puts it in compression, it drops out of that calculation (axial force 0).
trekSchijf.inactive: Inactive in this result: the member would be in compression and does not take part (axial force 0).
trekSchijf.diaphragmHint: Couples X, Y and the rotation about Z of the nodes as one rigid plane, like a floor with a structural topping. All nodes lie at the same height (within 1 mm); a node belongs to at most one diaphragm.
trekSchijf.nodeInDiaphragm: Belongs to {{name}} ({{count}} nodes, Z {{z}} mm): X, Y and the rotation about Z are rigidly coupled.

refused.tooFewNodes: Choose at least two nodes for a diaphragm.
refused.notLevel: Node {{low}} and node {{high}} differ {{mm}} mm in height; a diaphragm needs all nodes at the same height (within 1 mm).
refused.alreadyInDiaphragm: Node {{node}} already belongs to diaphragm {{id}}; a node belongs to at most one diaphragm.

trekSchijf.legendHint: Dashed and grey: tension-only members that would be in compression in this result and do not take part.
trekSchijf.crossRuleKept: Active because of the cross rule: without this member no diagonal of its cross would take part. It may carry a small compressive force.
trekSchijf.fitDeltaHint: Fitted after the permanent load: the stress-free length is L + Δ0.

bedding.title: Member on elastic foundation
bedding.modulusTitle: Modulus of subgrade reaction k for the vertical direction (global Z)
bedding.lateralTitle: Lateral modulus: horizontal, perpendicular to the member, on both sides; for a member steeper than 45° (a (raking) pile) all round, perpendicular to the member; empty = none
bedding.compressionOnly: Compression only (the soil takes no tension)
bedding.incomplete: Enter k (or the lateral k) and b greater than zero; otherwise no foundation is set.
bedding.hint: Line stiffness k·b (kN/m per m). The solver places springs k·b along the whole length and subdivides the member finely enough relative to the characteristic length 1/λ = (4EI/(k·b))^¼. The shorter the member compared with 1/λ, the more it settles as a rigid block.
bedding.compressionHint: Compression only: where the member lifts, the soil does not pull and the springs drop out; the solver finds the part in contact itself.
bedding.verticalHint: This member is (nearly) vertical: only a lateral foundation, like a pile in the ground. It acts all round, perpendicular to the pile.
bedding.verticalHasK: This member is (nearly) vertical but still has a vertical k: a vertical foundation is not possible there. Clear k and give only the lateral k.
bedding.allRoundHint: This member is steeper than 45°: the lateral foundation acts all round, perpendicular to the member, as for a raking pile.
bedding.verticalRefused: Member {{id}} would then be (nearly) vertical while it rests on a vertical foundation (k): a vertical foundation is not possible there. First remove the vertical k (lateral only, as for a pile) or remove the foundation.
bedding.mixed: The selected members have different foundations; a change applies to all of them.
bedding.noResult: The solver returned no foundation output for this result.

plateBedding.title: Plate on elastic foundation
plateBedding.modulusTitle: Modulus of subgrade reaction k, perpendicular to the plate
plateBedding.compressionOnly: Compression only (the soil takes no tension)
plateBedding.mixed: The selected plates have different foundations; a change applies to all of them.
plateBedding.hint: Winkler foundation, e.g. a ground floor slab on sand: the solver puts a spring k·A perpendicular to the plate on every node of the mesh. The soil lies on the underside (hatched, layer Supports). Without a support in the plane of the plate the solver holds it there as long as the load is perpendicular to the plate; a load in the plane of the plate (e.g. wind) needs a support.
plateBedding.compressionHint: Compression only: where the plate lifts, the soil does not pull and the springs drop out; the solver finds the part in contact itself.
plateBedding.wallSide: Wall: the soil lies on the {{side}} side (hatched, layer Supports). That side follows from the plate axes (on a wall the y axis points up) and cannot be chosen. If the soil is on the other side, settlement and ground pressure have the opposite sign.
plateBedding.wallCompression: Compression only on a wall is correct only if the soil really lies on the {{side}} side. If it is on the other side (in a basement, for two of the four walls), the soil lets go exactly where the wall pushes into it: calculate that wall without compression only.
plateBedding.noResult: The solver returned no plate foundation output for this result.

report.noSketch: No drawing available for this profile shape.
report.timberNote: Timber: E = E₀,mean (stiffness in the analysis); strength values per class follow from EN 338 / EN 14080 and are applied by the code check (EN 1995).
report.noLoadCases: No load cases in the model.
report.selfWeightIncluded: Self-weight of members with a recognized material and section is automatically included in this case (q = ρ·A·g per member).
report.selfWeightSkipped: Self-weight could not be determined for:
report.selfWeightOff: Self-weight is disabled — not included in the analysis.
report.selfWeightNoDeadCase: Self-weight is enabled, but there is no load case of type “Permanent”: self-weight is NOT included in the analysis.
report.selfWeightCaseNotDead: Self-weight is enabled, but the load case marked “self-weight” is not of type “Permanent”: self-weight is NOT included in the analysis.
report.noCombinations: No load combinations in the model.
report.sectionClt: Cross-laminated timber — layup and check per lamella
report.cltGeen: No cross-laminated timber members in the model (profile name "CLT …").
report.cltMethodeNoot: Method: composite section with rigid connection (NEN-EN 1995-1-1 Annex B with γ = 1) — only the longitudinal layers carry in the span direction, the cross layers form the shear connection. Check per lamella: bending cl. 6.1.6 and shear cl. 6.1.7 on the design values of that layer's strength class; rolling shear in the cross layers for information.
report.cltStaafKeuzeNoot: For {{aantal}} of the {{totaal}} CLT members the derivation has been omitted on request; those members are still listed in the check overview.
report.cltStijfheidKop: Effective bending stiffness (Annex B, rigid connection: γ = 1)
report.sectionBeton: Concrete — cross-section, M-κ diagram and N-M interaction diagram
report.betonGeen: No concrete members in the model (material a strength class such as "C30/37", profile a rectangle such as "300x500", plus a reinforcement cage in the member properties).
report.betonMethodeNoot: Method: cross-section check for bending with axial force to {{norm}}, in the ultimate limit state. Two checks at the same point: the rectangular stress distribution of 3.1.7(3) (the classic hand calculation) and the M-N-κ calculation with the parabola-rectangle diagram of 3.1.7(1), where M_Rd(N_Ed) is the largest moment on the M-κ diagram at N_Ed. Under compression the minimum eccentricity of 6.1(4) applies. Sign convention: N positive is tension, M positive is tension in the bottom fibre.
report.betonStaafKeuzeNoot: For {{aantal}} of the {{totaal}} concrete members the elaboration has been omitted on request; those members do appear in the check summary.
report.betonGeenToets: The calculation core returned no check for this member.
report.betonGeenKorf: The reinforcement cage could not be derived from the model or from the summary line; the cross-section drawing has therefore been omitted.
report.betonDoorsnedeBijschrift: Cross-section {{naam}} mm with reinforcement cage (true to scale).
report.betonMKappaBijschrift: M-κ diagram at N_Ed = {{n}} kN. M_Rd = {{mrd}} kNm at κ_u = {{ku}}·10⁻³/m.
report.betonInteractieBijschrift: N-M interaction diagram (failure envelope) with the design point (N_Ed; M_Ed) = ({{n}} kN; {{m}} kNm). The dashed line is the horizontal cut M_Rd(N_Ed) on which the unity check rests.
report.betonGeenInteractie: No interaction diagram available for this member.
report.betonBeperkingenKop: What this concrete check does not cover
report.betonBeperkingenInleiding: Only the CROSS-SECTION has been checked, for bending with axial force in the ultimate limit state, at the governing point of the envelope of the ULS combinations. Everything below is NOT checked; a concrete member that passes here has therefore not been fully verified.
report.betonNietDwarskracht: Shear. There is no check on V_Rd,c or V_Rd,s and no stirrup calculation. The stirrup in the drawing only sets the position of the main reinforcement; it has not been checked for shear.
report.betonNietTweedeOrde: Second-order effects with axial load. N_Ed and M_Ed come from the first-order analysis; there is no slenderness criterion, no method based on nominal stiffness (5.8.7) and no method based on nominal curvature (5.8.8). For a slender compression member this check is therefore on the UNSAFE side.
report.betonNietImperfecties: Geometric imperfections and lateral instability of slender beams.
report.betonNietKruip: Creep and shrinkage. The calculation uses φ = 0. In this ultimate cross-section check creep plays no part, but as soon as the force distribution depends on creep (second order, permanently loaded columns) that assumption is no longer safe.
report.betonNietBgt: The entire serviceability limit state: stress limitation, crack control and deflection control. NO crack width is calculated and there is no deflection check for concrete.
report.betonNietDetaillering: Detailing: bar spacing, anchorage of longitudinal reinforcement and the minimum and maximum reinforcement areas for beams (9.2.1.1) and columns (9.5.2). A cage that passes the cross-section check may therefore still contain too little or too much reinforcement.
report.betonNietDekking: The minimum cover c_min for an exposure class IS checked against the code, but on input rather than in this member check: the section chooser and the Code tab compare the specified c_nom with c_min,dur from table 4.4N (in the version prescribed by the Dutch national annex) and the bond requirement of table 4.2. That result does not appear in this report, and without a chosen exposure class there is no check at all. Also outside the scope: the structural class per table 4.3N (it is input, not derived), the allowance for aggregate larger than 32 mm, uneven surfaces (4.4.1.2(11)) and abrasion classes XM1 to XM3.
report.betonBeperkingVorm: a rectangle b × h, a T or an L, with bending about the strong axis. Biaxial bending (art. 5.8.9) is checked for a rectangular column with art. 5.8 data: the imperfection and the second-order effect about the z-axis and the interaction (5.39); not for a T or L. Other cross-section shapes are not checked. For a T or L the calculation additionally rests on the assumptions listed with each member's cross-section.
report.betonBeperkingUc: About the unity check itself: it is determined as M_Ed / M_Rd(N_Ed) — a horizontal cut through the interaction diagram at the design value of the axial force — and NOT as the distance from the design point to the failure envelope. For a member whose N and M increase together in the same combination, that measure gives a more favourable picture than a radial measure would. The interaction diagram is there to make that ratio visible, not to read the UC from.
report.betonTweedeOrdeGedaan: Second-order effects under axial loading HAVE been included: the internal forces were determined with the general method of 5.8.6 — geometrically and materially non-linear, with the secant bending stiffness per segment taken from the M-N-κ diagram. N_Ed and M_Ed in this cross-section check therefore come from that analysis and not from a first-order analysis. The simplified methods based on nominal stiffness (5.8.7) and nominal curvature (5.8.8) were consequently not used. The segment tables, the convergence trace and the assumptions are in the chapter “Concrete — physically non-linear second order”.
report.betonBeperkingenTweedeOrdeUitzondering: With one exception: the second-order effects of 5.8 WERE included in this analysis — see item 5.8 below and the chapter with the segment tables.
report.eisNietGerekend: No materially non-linear analysis was run. This chapter fills once the analysis type "2nd order + non-linear material" is selected and the model contains concrete members with a reinforcement cage; the segment stiffnesses then come from the calculation engine.
report.eisMethodeNoot: Method: the general method of NEN-EN 1992-1-1 5.8.6. Every concrete member is divided into segments and equilibrium and compatibility are satisfied at the midpoint of each segment (5.8.6(6)); this yields the curvature κ per segment at the internal forces found (N_Ed, M_Ed) and the secant bending stiffness EI = (M_Ed − M₀)/κ, with which the frame is solved again until the stiffnesses no longer change. Sign convention: N positive is tension, M positive is tension in the bottom fibre.
report.eisGeenOmhullende: The stiffness follows from the internal forces of a single load state, so every combination has its own EI distribution and there is no envelope stiffness: superposition is invalid in this path, both geometrically and physically.
report.eisAlleCombinaties: All {{n}} combinations analysed with non-linear material are shown below; select a single combination in the sidebar to show only that one.
report.eisOvergeslagenKop: {{n}} concrete member(s) did NOT take part in the materially non-linear analysis and kept the uncracked stiffness E_cm·I_c of the gross cross-section — for those members the result is that of the geometric second order (P-Δ) alone:
report.eisSegmentlengteWaarde: requested {{doel}} mm; actual {{echt}} mm ({{aantal}} segments on the longest member). Division rule: {{regel}}
report.eisRondenWaarde: {{n}} frame solution(s) after the segment division (round 0). Each round: solve, send (N, M) per segment to the engine, receive the new EI. The tables below show the LAST round — the internal forces the frame was solved with, and the EI that follows from them; that EI differs from the EI used to obtain those forces by at most the tolerance.
report.eisGehaald: achieved: {{waarde}} % in the last round (member {{staaf}}, segment {{segment}})
report.eisGeklemd: {{n}} segment(s) clamped at that lower bound; a clamped value is a numerical lower bound and not a calculation result.
report.eisKruip519: ULS: φ_ef = φ(∞,t₀)·M₀Eqp/M₀Ed per member (5.8.4(2) (5.19)), first-order moments at the section with the largest |M₀Ed| (5.8.4(3)); the derivation is given with the member.
report.eisZonderKruipKop: CALCULATED WITHOUT CREEP — member(s) {{ids}}: no creep coefficient φ(∞,t₀) was given (cl. 3.1.4), so φ_ef = 0.
report.eisZonderKruipUitleg: Cl. 5.8.6(4) allows creep to be taken into account by multiplying all strain values of the stress-strain diagram by (1 + φ_ef); for the initial slope this amounts to the effective modulus of elasticity E_c,eff = E_cm/(1 + φ) of (7.20). Without that reduction the bending stiffness is too high: the calculated deflection is TOO SMALL, and in a statically indeterminate structure the overly stiff concrete members also attract too much moment. Both are on the unsafe side. Specify φ(∞,t₀), or have it calculated according to annex B from the relative humidity, the age t₀ at loading and the cement class (h₀ follows from the cross-section).
report.eisFiguurBijschrift: Bending stiffness EI per segment along member {{staaf}}. The dashed line is the uncracked E_c·I_c = {{ei0}} kNm²; {{gescheurd}} of the {{totaal}} segments are cracked. Lowest value {{min}} kNm² ({{factor}}·E_c·I_c).
report.eisM0Uitleg: M₀ is the moment at κ = 0. The moment is taken about the geometric mid-fibre h/2 and not about the plastic centroid, so for an asymmetric reinforcement cage under compression M(κ = 0) is not zero; the secant is therefore EI = (M_Ed − M₀)/κ and not M_Ed/κ. The column EI / E_cI_c relates that stiffness to the uncracked E_c·I_c = {{ei0}} kNm² — in the ultimate limit state a comparison value and not a design value, because 5.8.6(5) omits the concrete tension and then no uncracked branch exists.
report.eisUgtToelichting: In this variant the State column only says whether |M_Ed| exceeds the cracking moment |M_cr|. The stiffness itself is determined without concrete tension in both cases (5.8.6(5)): as soon as tension occurs in the cross-section EI is below E_c·I_c, even for a segment marked as uncracked, whereas a segment in which the axial force keeps the whole cross-section in compression stays close to E_c·I_c.
report.eisBgtToelichting: In this variant ζ of (7.19) interpolates between the uncracked and the fully cracked state (7.4.3): ζ = 0 is uncracked, ζ → 1 fully cracked.
report.eisRatioBoven1: A ratio above 1 can occur: E_c·I_c is the gross concrete cross-section only, whereas the reinforcement contributes in the uncracked state.
report.sectionSpanning: Stress check — cross-section and stress distribution
report.spanningGeen: No members with a free material in the model (material name "VRIJ:…").
report.spanningMethodeNoot: Method: the stresses follow directly from the internal forces — σx = N/A + My·(z − zc)/Iy and τ = Vz·S(z)/(Iy·b(z)) — and are combined per fibre over the depth into the von Mises equivalent stress for a plane stress state: σeq = √(σx² + σz² − σx·σz + 3·τ²). At σz = 0 this reduces to √(σx² + 3·τ²), the form given in NEN-EN 1993-1-1 6.2.1(5). This is explicitly NOT a code check: there is no cross-section classification and no buckling, lateral-torsional buckling or deflection check, and the permissible stress is supplied by the user.
report.spanningStaafKeuzeNoot: For {{aantal}} of the {{totaal}} members the derivation has been omitted on request; those members are still listed in the check overview.
report.spanningFiguurBijschrift: Cross-section with the stress distribution at the governing section (x = {{x}} mm, combination {{combo}}): N = {{n}} kN, Vz = {{v}} kN, My = {{m}} kNm. Tension positive; the dashed line in the right-hand panel is fd = {{fd}} N/mm².
report.ketenKop: Derivation according to the National Annex, step by step:
report.verloopNoot: Dimensions vary linearly from {{begin}} at x = 0 to {{eind}} at x = L. Every cross-section check was carried out at all {{aantal}} evaluation points using the local cross-section; six of them are listed below, plus — marked with * after the position — the governing evaluation point.
report.verloopMaatgevend: Governing point: x = {{x}} mm (t = {{t}}), check {{toets}}, UC = {{uc}}.
report.verloopStabiliteit: Cross-section used for the stability checks
report.verloopSectieNoot: Tapered member: these members vary from {{begin}} to {{eind}}. The properties below are those of the starting profile; the cross-sections along the member are given with the check of each member.
report.notComputed: Not yet computed — run the analysis via Calculate. Earlier results are discarded automatically after any model change.
report.schemaLegend: Node numbers black, member numbers grey in parentheses; dimensions in m, loads characteristic per load case (G/Q/S/W).
report.schemaLegendAanzicht: Members are shown in elevation at true size, around their system line: the outline over the section depth, the flange lines, hidden lines dashed (inner wall of hollow sections, the web of a section about its weak axis), schematic laminations for glued laminated timber, and for concrete the bar layers at their cover with the stirrups at their spacing.
report.schemaLegendKipsteunen: Lateral restraints as used by the checks: a small triangle on the restrained flange (for an upright member the top flange is the left side), an open diamond for a restraint from the timber restraint spacing, a fork where the member end is taken as a fork support.
report.envelopeBandNote: Envelope: per member the band between minimum and maximum over all combinations.
report.reactionSignNote: Sign convention: Fx positive to the right, Fz positive upwards (reaction on the structure).
report.noReactions: No supports with reactions in the model.
report.fieldDeflNote: w = deflection perpendicular to the member axis, taken from left to right (a vertical member from base to top): negative = sagging, for a vertical member towards the right; x measured from the left end or the base.
report.governingDispNote: Envelope selected — showing the governing combination (largest displacement):
report.plateStressNote: Stresses in N/mm², element-averaged over the analysis mesh; min/max per plate — the same values as the contour legend on the canvas. The governing element is the element with the largest von Mises stress.
report.plateStressMaterialNote: σ₁ along main direction 1 (the grain; for cross-laminated timber the longitudinal layers), σ₂ perpendicular to it and τ₁₂, computed from σx, σy and τxy with the main direction θ of the plate: σ₁ = σx·cos²θ + σy·sin²θ + 2·τxy·sinθ·cosθ. Timber and cross-laminated timber only; the strengths of a timber check belong to these axes.
report.sectionsHint2: Checkbox: include or not. Name: jump to it.
report.sectionsHintNvt: Struck through: this model cannot fill that chapter, so it is left out of the report. Hover it for the reason.
report.tocLeeg: No chapters yet — enable sections in the sidebar.

report.rapportTypeBeperktHint: The essentials for the client: assumptions, sketch, results and the check overview.
report.rapportTypeHint: A preset: every section below can still be switched on or off individually.

report.staafKeuzeHint: Only the ticked members get their derivations in the report; the check overview always lists every member.
report.staafKeuzeSectieUit: The chapter “Checks per member” is switched off — enable it below for this selection to take effect.
report.staafKeuzeNoot: For {{aantal}} of the {{totaal}} checked members the detailed output was left out on request; those members do appear in the check overview.
report.staafKeuzeLeeg: No member was selected for detailed output — tick at least one member in the report sidebar.
report.zoomHint: Holding Ctrl while scrolling zooms the report as well.
report.beffInleiding: Flange width entered {{ingevoerd}} mm; the calculation used b_eff = {{beff}} mm. The beam line this member belongs to has {{aantal}} span(s) ({{spans}}), start {{start}}, end {{eind}}. The member midpoint is at x = {{x}} mm along that line.
report.beffStaven: The beam line consists of members {{staven}}; the supports are at nodes {{knopen}}.
report.beffStaafEnkel: The beam line is this single member; the supports are at nodes {{knopen}}.
report.beffZonesNoot: b_eff differs per region. This member uses a single value, that of the region containing the member midpoint; 5.3.2.1(4) permits a constant width per span, taking the value applicable to the span section. Over a support b_eff is smaller than the value used, so the cross-section has been taken as too stiff there.
report.beffMislukt: The effective flange width was NOT derived: {{reden}}. The calculation used the flange width entered, {{breedte}} mm. Per 5.3.2.1(3) the effective width is at most equal to the actual flange width and usually smaller; using the full width is therefore on the unsafe side.
report.betonNietSpreidingTrekwapening: The DISTRIBUTION of tension reinforcement over the effective flange width. NOTE 2 to 9.2.1.2(1) states that at intermediate supports of continuous beams the total area of tension reinforcement A_s of a flanged cross-section should be spread over the effective flange width (see 5.3.2), part of it may be concentrated over the web width (figure 9.1). The reinforcement cage in this model has two rows — one top, one bottom, each across the width present at its own height — and therefore cannot express that distribution. Over a support the cage checked is thus a different cage from the one 9.2.1.2 prescribes.
report.betonNietBeffPerSegment: b_eff does NOT step within a member. A single value per member was used: that of the region containing the member midpoint. 5.3.2.1(4) permits this — “for structural analysis, where great accuracy is not required, a constant width may be assumed over the whole span” — but over a support b_eff per figure 5.2 is considerably smaller, so the cross-section has been taken as TOO STIFF there. Too stiff gives too little deflection and too little second-order effect: the unsafe side. The per-member region table shows how much it matters.
report.betonKetenVerwijzing: The full derivation of this check — {{aantal}} steps, each with formula, substituted values, reference and the underlying assumptions — is given in the chapter “Check per member”, at the detailed level.
report.eisFiguurTitel: Flexural stiffness EI along member {{staaf}}, with the uncracked E_c·I_c as reference line
report.eisAnalysetypeFysisch: Second order, geometrically and materially non-linear: as P-Δ, but the concrete members receive the secant EI per segment from the calculation engine (NEN-EN 1992-1-1 5.8.6). Without concrete members with a reinforcement cage the result equals second-order (P-Δ).

report.cltSomIefNet: Σ over the longitudinal layers = I_ef,net
report.cltIefNetGelijk: All longitudinal layers have the same modulus of elasticity (E_ref = {{e}} N/mm²), so the geometric sum Σ(I_i + A_i·a_i²) equals I_ef,net = (EI)_ef/E_ref. I_ef,net is a comparison quantity against a solid cross-section; the check uses (EI)_ef itself.
report.cltIefNetAfwijkend: The longitudinal layers do NOT have the same modulus of elasticity, so the geometric sum Σ(I_i + A_i·a_i²) = {{som}}·10⁶ mm⁴ does not equal I_ef,net = (EI)_ef/E_ref = {{ief}}·10⁶ mm⁴ with E_ref = {{e}} N/mm² (the top longitudinal layer). I_ef,net is a comparison quantity; the check uses (EI)_ef itself.
report.cltFiguurBijschriftPunten: Layup from top to bottom, with the bending stress σm,d (tension positive) and the shear stress τd over the depth. NOTE: the two stress panels belong to TWO DIFFERENT points in the envelope — σm,d at the governing moment point (My,Ed = {{m}} kNm{{mx}}), τd at the governing shear force point (Vz,Ed = {{v}} kN{{vx}}). Drawn side by side, but together NOT a state of a single cross-section.

staalhal.knopHint: Create a complete steel or timber hall as a 3D frame with a wizard: frames, purlins, bracing, foundation and loads.

afmetingen.hint: Axes: x along the hall, y across, z up; level 0 is the column base. Frame and purlin spacing are maxima: the layout is divided equally.

profielen.hint: Columns are rotated 90° (web in the frame plane). Purlins, eaves beams and bracing are pinned at both ends.

verbanden.dak: Roof bracing: cross in every purlin field
verbanden.wanden: Wall bracing: cross in both side walls
verbanden.kopgevels: Gable bracing: cross in both end walls
verbanden.hint: With pinned column bases, wall bracing is needed for longitudinal stability.

fundering.diepte: Depth of beam axis below level 0
fundering.hint: Longitudinal beams run under both column lines. Every column has a pile, with piles in between at no more than the pile spacing. If the grid lies below level 0, a concrete pedestal connects the column base to the grid. Hall and grid are analysed together.

belastingen.hint: Roof loads per m² of horizontal projection, as line loads on the purlins. A roof imposed load above zero gets its own Q case (category H). Transverse wind acts on the columns and as suction on the roof; longitudinal wind on the gable.
belastingen.afgeleid: q_p = {{qp}} kN/m² at {{ze}} m; pressure {{druk}}, suction {{zuiging}}, longitudinal {{langs}}, roof {{dak}} kN/m².
